solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expert about to break best form of digital security

indicators.note: one piece breaks into another, splitting it apart

parts.note: to best someone is to top them

indicators.note: about signals the word for expert is turned round

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Talk of top-class protection for computer data, as if from a cybersecurity advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means relating to the digits, here the toes, not computers; 'about' reverses the expert word before 'to break' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel cap on a boot protects the toes, the foot's digits.

clue.text: Funny (not the first) thing astronomer looks into

indicators.note: the bracketed phrase tells us to drop the opening letter of the synonym

parts.note: jocular means funny or joking

explanation.surface: A quip about something comic that a stargazer peers into.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocular is the eyepiece of a telescope, the part an observer puts an eye to.

clue.text: Church carries on with limited money agreement

indicators.note: the church abbreviation carries the other letters within it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter of the money word goes

parts.note: currency is money

explanation.surface: The church keeps going despite tight funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' means the church letters C and E hold everything else; 'limited' drops the money word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurrence is accord between parties, a meeting of minds.

clue.text: Broadcast quiet Mass in appropriate city?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: in places the mass unit within the city's name

parts.note: Rome, seat of the Pope, is a fitting city for a Mass
a gram is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: A broadcast of a quiet Mass from a fitting city such as Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks religious but is the physical quantity; Rome is 'appropriate' because it is the home of the Catholic Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a broadcast show on radio or television.

clue.text: Home Office fight to keep Queen's English trailer

indicators.note: the outer letters keep the others held inside them

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK interior ministry
to box is to fight
R (Regina) is Queen, plus S for the possessive

explanation.surface: A government department squabbling over correct English on a film trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Office is the UK ministry for policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsebox is a trailer or van built for carrying horses.

clue.text: Help boy, offering practical experience

parts.note: to hand someone something, or give a hand, is to help
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A father getting his lad to lend a hand, so he learns by doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands-on describes learning or work done directly, in person, rather than in theory.

clue.text: Revolver to go off above soldiers

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to rot is to go off, decay
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A gun that may fail, sitting above a band of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a pistol but is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Withdraw European books

parts.note: B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: An order to pull European books from sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it goes back, so to ebb is to recede or retreat.

clue.text: Catch bird interrupting deliveries

indicators.note: the bird breaks into the cricket word, splitting it

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries (balls bowled)
a rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A bird swoops in to stop a fielder's catch, or the post.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a cricket term: one bowler's set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch something said by others, unintentionally, is to overhear it.

clue.text: Refuse vessel originally donated in settlement

indicators.note: in puts the pieces within the settlement word

parts.note: a town is a settlement
an urn is a vessel

indicators.note: originally points at the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Refusing a gift of a vase for the village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as rubbish, a noun, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to decline or reject it.

clue.text: Computer fit to be installed in Times

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside the times symbols

parts.note: T is time, so TT is times
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A computer that is ready to be set up at the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper; it is two T's.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat touchscreen computing device.

clue.text: Berlin agreement to protect tailless wild cat

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: the tail, the last letter, is removed

parts.note: to guard is to protect

explanation.surface: A treaty signed in Berlin protects a wild cat that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a large spotted big cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Like a hair shirt? Remove yours at the outset

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw or remove, as from a race

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Advice to take off an itchy penitent's garment straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair shirt is made of coarse cloth that irritates the skin, making it itchy.

clue.text: The right doctor assembled emergency room gauge

parts.note: R is right
MO is a medical officer
met means came together, assembled
ER is an emergency room

explanation.surface: A doctor gathering kit for the casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermometer is an instrument measuring temperature.

clue.text: Old figure? MCC has a few!

definitions.meaning: a numeral of ancient Rome, an old way of writing a number
MCC, 1200, is made of three such letter numerals

explanation.walkthrough: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, the English cricket authority, but here it is the number 1200.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Romans wrote numbers with letters like M and C, so these are old figures.

clue.text: Ten men with current force in Brussels turned up, to find eg Henry?

indicators.note: in places the pieces within the Brussels letters
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU
X is the Roman numeral ten
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
I is the symbol for electric current
the CID is the detective branch of a police force

explanation.surface: A team, with electricity and power, rising in the EU capital, as a clue to a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes UE, which surrounds XORICID. Henry VIII had two of his wives beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxoricide is wife-killing, or one who kills his wife, as Henry VIII did.

clue.text: Hotel contributed to rustic game

indicators.note: the letter is added in, contributing to the countryman word

parts.note: a rustic is a peasant
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel adds a country game dish to its menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasant is a game bird shot for sport and food.

clue.text: In which Thor must rend ground?

definitions.text: In which Thor must rend ground?

indicators.note: ground as in broken up, so the words are reworked

explanation.surface: The Norse thunder god must tear up the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the earth Thor rends; it is the anagram signal. The whole clue also describes the storm, Thor being the thunder god.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor wields thunder, so a violent storm is where he tears the ground apart.

clue.text: Difficult spot in which to turn left

indicators.note: the spotting word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: to spy is to spot, catch sight of

indicators.note: to turn means the word for left reads backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A tricky place to make a left turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' reads as a place but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroppy person is bad-tempered and awkward to deal with.

clue.text: Actors on tour platoon picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the sound matters

parts.note: a troop is a platoon-like unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers picked up by a touring company.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a travelling company of performers.

clue.text: About to furnish Arab table full of dates

parts.note: ca (circa) means about
to lend is to furnish, give
Ar is short for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Supplying an Arab host with a table laden with dates.
explanation.walkthrough: The dates look like fruit on a table; they are days on a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a chart of the days and months of the year.

clue.text: A pal in New York tipping one crude source

indicators.note: tipping over turns the letters upside down in a down entry

parts.note: bud is American slang for a pal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An American friend leaves a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai, in the Gulf, made its fortune from oil, a source of crude.

clue.text: Wall in green, at shed

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the small word comes out

parts.note: green means immature, inexperienced

explanation.surface: Building a wall in a green beside a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a hut; it is a verb meaning lose.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure someone is to shut or wall them up.

clue.text: Graduates gather round old British tree

indicators.note: the graduates surround the letter for old

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so BABA is two graduates
O is old
B is British

explanation.surface: Graduates gathering round an old British tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree with a huge swollen trunk.

clue.text: Drill to polish up

indicators.note: up, in a down answer, means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: An instruction to polish a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A bur is a small rotary cutting tool used by dentists.

clue.text: Show ID to protect old solicitor

indicators.note: the identification number protects, encloses, the letter

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number
O is old
a tout solicits custom

explanation.surface: Presenting identification to shield an elderly lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer; here it is one who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out is to show or indicate.

clue.text: Tiny tree, gnarled for yonks

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A tiny, twisted tree that has stood for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yonks' is British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks means ages, and an eternity is an extremely long time.

clue.text: Trainee's heading off for a profitable job

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, goes off

parts.note: a learner is a trainee; the 's is 'is' linking to the pieces

explanation.surface: A trainee goes off to a lucrative post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a nice little earner' is British slang for a money-making job.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is something that brings in income.
